question: In this machine, must every spare index whose lease was closed with reason 'Swap' have its intent pod 'Gone' in every reachable state — i.e. can a swap-consumed spare index ever hold a Live pod again?
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: Capacity consumed by a node-failure swap is spent: the funded slot now carries the swapped-in active work, so that index must never be re-populated with a standby pod.

question: Should the number of Live spare pods never exceed the declared spare count (3) minus the number of spares already consumed by a swap?
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: Standby capacity is funded from a fixed cover: live spares plus consumed spares can never exceed the declared spare budget, or the run over-subscribes its gang cover.

question: Once an index's lease closure reason is 'Swap', must it stay 'Swap' forever — is any transition allowed to rewrite it back to 'None'?
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: A closed lease's closure reason is write-once; rewriting it is a history rewrite the transition checker rejects (INV-CLOSED-MONOTONE).

question: Should an external pod deletion (eviction/drain) leave every closure reason untouched — in particular never mark the lost index as 'Swap'-consumed?

norm: Losing a pod to an eviction or drain is a recoverable absence, not a promotion; only a node-failure swap closes a spare lease with reason 'Swap'.

question: Can a node-failure swap only consume an index that currently has a Live spare pod (and whose reason is still 'None')?

norm: A swap lands on real, funded standby capacity: there must be a live spare with an open lease for it to consume, and a lease can only be closed once.

question: Must SwapConsume(idx) leave exactly that index with reason 'Swap' and pod 'Gone'?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'SwapConsume' || !data || data.idx === undefined || (post['reason'+data.idx] === 'Swap' && post['pod'+data.idx] === 'Gone')
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: Promotion of a spare atomically retires the spare: its pod leaves the standby set and its lease closes with reason 'Swap'.

question: After a TopUp, must every index that has not been swap-consumed hold a Live spare pod?

domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: Reconciliation is convergent: a single top-up restores the full declared standby set minus whatever the swaps legitimately consumed.

question: Is TopUp purely additive — can it ever take an index from Live to Gone?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => pre['pod'+i] !== 'Live' || post['pod'+i] === 'Live')
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: A top-up only fills genuinely-missing slots; it never deletes or disturbs a healthy standby pod.

question: Must TopUp leave every index whose reason is already 'Swap' with pod 'Gone', even when the consumed index is numerically lower than a surviving spare (the count-vs-name mismatch of #91)?
js: (pre, action, data, post) => action !== 'TopUp' || [0,1,2].every(i => pre['reason'+i] !== 'Swap' || post['pod'+i] === 'Gone')
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: emitSparePods subtracts consumedSpareCount from the target but still fills indices 0..count-1, so a swap-consumed LOW index is re-created while a surviving HIGH index is skipped by name.

question: Does the name-keyed presence map guarantee that TopUp leaves every already-Live spare index exactly as it was, never rebuilding an index a survivor still owns?
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: Presence is keyed by sparePodName(run,i) rather than a raw count, so a present index is skipped and never duplicated into two pods/leases of one name.

norm: emitSparePods only reads lease closure state (consumedSpareCount) and writes pods; it must never mutate a lease's ClosureReason.

norm: findSpareLease pairs a swap with the one spare covering the failed rank's group, so a swap consumes exactly one spare slot.

question: Should the number of indices marked 'Swap' be non-decreasing across every transition, so consumedSpareCount never shrinks and the top-up target never grows back?
domain: Kubernetes/GPU run controller — standby (spare) capacity reconciliation
norm: consumedSpareCount is derived from closed leases with reason 'Swap'; those slots are gone for good, so the count is monotone non-decreasing.
